suggestions.title: 12 Angry Men
suggestions.description: Eleven jurors are ready to convict a boy accused of murder. One man votes not guilty — not because he is sure, but because a life deserves a real conversation. Sidney Lumet's debut traps twelve strangers (and you) in one sweltering room, turning a single word — 'guilty' — into the greatest moral battleground in cinema. Shot in under three weeks on a tiny budget, it proves all you need is a sharp argument and twelve chairs. A flawless 9.0 classic that feels more urgent than ever.

suggestions.title: Back to the Future
suggestions.description: Marty McFly accidentally punches a modified DeLorean to 1955 — and must now make his own teenage parents fall in love, or he will literally erase himself from existence. Robert Zemeckis's clockwork-perfect script, Christopher Lloyd's gloriously unhinged Doc Brown, and one of the great endings in blockbuster history make this the definitive '80s adventure. Effortlessly funny, endlessly rewatchable, and 8.5-rated proof that a time-travel movie can be pure joy.

suggestions.title: The Prestige
suggestions.description: Two rival Victorian magicians — Robert Angier and Alfred Borden — escalate a duel over the perfect illusion until obsession consumes everything in their path. Christopher Nolan builds this film like a magic trick itself: every scene a setup, every detail a sleight of hand, the final reveal landing like a thunderclap. Hugh Jackman, Christian Bale and Michael Caine at the top of their game in the most elegantly constructed thriller of the 2000s. A 8.5-rated puzzle box that begs for an immediate rewatch.
